questions.prompt: For which values of parameter a does the equation √(x+2) + √(x+5) = a have exactly two distinct real solutions?
questions.explanation: The left side f(x)=√(x+2)+√(x+5) has domain x≥-2. It's strictly increasing (derivative positive), so f is one-to-one. Range is [f(-2),∞) = [√3,∞). For any a in the range, exactly one solution exists. Thus exactly two distinct solutions never occur.
questions.expectedAnswer: No such values of a exist
choices: No such values of a exist

questions.prompt: The equation |x² - 4x + 3| = a has exactly three distinct real solutions. What is the value of a?
questions.explanation: Let g(x)=x²-4x+3=(x-1)(x-3). Vertex at x=2 gives g(2)=-1. The V-shaped absolute value reflects negative portion upward, creating a local maximum at x=2 with value 1. For horizontal line y=a: 0 solutions when a<0; 2 solutions when a=0 or a>1; 4 solutions when 0<a<1; exactly 3 solutions when a=1 (touches at vertex and intersects twice on outer branches).

bank_prepared.prompt: The equation |x² - 4x + 3| = a has exactly three distinct real solutions. What is the value of a?
bank_prepared.explanation: Setting |x²-4x+3|=a splits into two quadratics. Exactly three solutions arise when one quadratic has two distinct roots and the other has a repeated root (touching zero), which occurs only at a=1.
